page.notes: Several black-letter words are read with some doubt; I am not certain of the German spellings in the declension of "Sein" and in the "Abl." lines. Possible misreadings: "in e" (in the first paragraph, and "in e assumunt" in the second) and the sign "n" after "assumunt" and "pluralibus" may be printers' marks rather than letters. The line "die brußte den brüsten" is read as printed but may be a printing error. The first line is a fragment carried over from the previous page, with its opening cut off at the left edge. The last line is cut off at the lower right edge.
